analysis:
Examined both startup files' complete supplied BASE/HEAD source, shutdown patch and metadata, and testing patch/metadata against the canonical index and supplied T-041 detail. No independently supported security regression in this scope. ProviderLoop+StartupPreload.swift:302-308 now queues memory/slot-skipped candidates for recovery, excluding cancellation, shutdown and supervisor stop. Existing no-eviction preload admission, self-test retirement hash binding and coordinator unadvertisement remain unchanged. Integration must examine ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery: selection filtering, retry bounds, serialized memory admission, self-test handling and servingDrain/add-on hold checks; the new enqueue condition does not itself check servingDrain, but the recovery implementation is not supplied here (A-018, TB-012, T-059, T-029).
ProviderLoop+StartupShutdown.swift:61,78-96 replaces indefinite unload waiting with a 15-second per-slot wait and retains unfinished unload tasks/slots. Admission closure, App Attest worker stop, inflight cancellation and native MiMo drain precede this change. Shutdown now returns true even with resident slots and may reach MLX.Memory.clearCache at line 63 while an unload remains active. Verify callers actually exit rather than restart/reuse the loop, and verify native retirement/cache-reclamation safety with outstanding tasks (TB-007, T-028, T-010; logout process-stop contract A-008/T-053). Supplied source does not establish a misuse or unsafe native operation. ProviderLoop+Testing.swift:514-522 adds internal override/wait seams, not a demonstrated remote entry point. No changed encryption, cache salt/SSD storage, billing, artifact qualification or serving authorization logic is visible. Remaining lifecycle and recovery contracts require cross-file integration, not findings inferred from missing source.
